solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put out pole with end disappearing in river

indicators.note: in means the shortened pole is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: with end disappearing tells us to drop the final letter of the word for pole

parts.note: a pole is a post

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a pole out while punting, its tip vanishing into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to put them out of office, remove them from power.

clue.text: Representatives providing instruction to get rid of barriers

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark instructing that something be deleted
gates are barriers

explanation.surface: Delegates are given an order to tear down barriers.
explanation.walkthrough: DELE is printers' Latin for 'delete', the mark an editor puts beside text to be struck out.
explanation.definitionFit: Delegates are people sent to act or vote on behalf of others.

clue.text: Mostly professional gang in pre-flood operation?

indicators.note: mostly says the word for professional loses its last letter

parts.note: a paid player is a professional, not an amateur
a ring is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: A gang of pros carries out an operation before the flood arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: before the Flood, Noah led the animals into the Ark two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's task before the deluge was matching animals in twos, a job of coupling them up.

clue.text: Most wise and godly person having a long time inside

indicators.note: having here pairs with inside: the saint abbreviation holds something
inside says the long time goes within the saint abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a godly person
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: The wisest of all is a holy man who has lived for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage means wise, so its superlative means wisest of all.

clue.text: Stout knocked back with cheese? That's the stuff!

indicators.note: knocked back, like a drink downed, signals that the word for stout is read backwards

parts.note: stout means fat
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A pint of stout downed with some cheese: just what one needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' and 'knocked back' suggest a drink, and 'That's the stuff!' an exclamation of satisfaction; stuff here means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and taffeta is a crisp silk fabric.

clue.text: A number of men giving voice in concert

parts.note: ten is a number
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Several men sing together in a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor is the high male singing voice heard in choirs and concerts.

clue.text: Lorries in boring county

parts.note: flat means dull or boring
Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Trucks are found in some dull English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is the short form of Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatbeds are trucks with an open, flat platform for carrying loads.

clue.text: Go mad in hospital department building in need of oxygen

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

indicators.note: in need of means the building is lacking, so the oxygen symbol is taken out

parts.note: a house is a building
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A hospital ward runs short of oxygen and the staff go crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To go mad about something is to rave over it, to gush with excitement.

clue.text: A weird roofless home for bird in US

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so roofless removes the first letter of the word for weird

parts.note: eerie means weird

explanation.surface: An odd house without a roof shelters an American bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American spelling of eyrie, an eagle's nest high on a crag.

clue.text: Mess about before social event or cooperate?

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: to play is to mess about
a ball is a formal dance, a social event

explanation.surface: Fooling around before a party, or else working together?
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to work along with others.

clue.text: Inclined to be mendacious

explanation.surface: Disposed to tell fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is horizontal or reclining; the other is telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Royal house near castle mostly dilapidated

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling to ruin, so the letters are knocked into a new order
mostly means the word castle loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A royal residence stands beside a crumbling castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims castle to CASTL; 'dilapidated' rearranges NEAR plus CASTL.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was an English royal dynasty, rivals of York in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: One with negative response wins against a second person, right?

parts.note: gains means wins
ye is the old second-person pronoun, you

explanation.surface: Someone saying no gains the upper hand over a second person, correct?
explanation.definitionFit: A gainsayer is someone who contradicts or denies, a naysayer.

clue.text: One of Caesar's last words, the beast!

definitions.meaning: a wild animal or savage person

explanation.surface: Caesar's dying cry at his betrayer: you animal!
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin vocative of Brutus is the word Caesar speaks; a beast is also a savage creature.

clue.text: Country became backward, finishing with nothing

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for became from right to left

parts.note: got means became, as in got angry
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A nation slid backwards and ended up with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a West African nation lying between Ghana and Benin.

clue.text: Special gear enthusiast brought to plant, having crossed yard

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

indicators.note: having crossed means the plant spans across the yard abbreviation, taking it inside

parts.note: cress is a plant

explanation.surface: A fan carries a plant across the yard wearing special kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Costumes worn to a themed party are special clothing, gear in a playful sense.

clue.text: Covers food in tin with ordinary salt

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: in places the food inside the tin and seaman letters

parts.note: a salt is a sailor; OS stands for ordinary seaman
a pie is food

explanation.surface: A recipe: put the food in a tin with some table salt and cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordinary salt' reads as table salt, but a salt is a sailor and OS is an ordinary seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopies are overhead coverings such as awnings or the cover over a bed.

clue.text: Most genuine from the time of leading others

indicators.note: leading puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: since means from the time of
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: The most honest person, ever since they began leading the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine or heartfelt, so its superlative is most heartfelt.

clue.text: Gentleman with power rising in authentic act of revenge

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pieces inside the word for authentic

parts.note: real means authentic

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a gentleman or knight
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A knight rising to power commits a genuine act of vengeance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is a retaliatory act, a getting even.

clue.text: Using a tool to shift support across hole

indicators.note: across means the support stretches across the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
a hole is a squalid dwelling, a hovel

explanation.surface: Working with a tool to move a support over a hole in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole' looks like a pit to dig, but it means a dump of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Shovelling is moving material such as earth or snow with a spade-like implement.

clue.text: Discourteous old worker squashing females

indicators.note: squashing means the two pieces press around the females, holding them between

parts.note: a hand is a worker
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A rude old labourer crushes some women.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand behaviour is curt and casual, lacking politeness.

clue.text: Inadequate side dish

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word for side loses its last letter

parts.note: a flank is a side

explanation.surface: A disappointing side dish at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side dish' reads as one phrase, but 'side' is wordplay and 'dish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open tart, a sweet or savoury baked dish.

clue.text: Top man in his field, perhaps, spouting?

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field
a king is the top man

explanation.surface: The leader in his field, perhaps, mouthing off?
explanation.walkthrough: The top man in a lea would be its king, read cryptically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leaking lets liquid escape, spouting out through a hole.

clue.text: To roar out? That could suit me

definitions.text: To roar out? That could suit me

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of to roar are worked out into a different order

explanation.surface: A public speaker remarks that bellowing loudly would suit them fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rousing public speaker might well roar, so roaring suits such a declaimer.

clue.text: Ending in jail, I am afraid of getting no answer — am I there for ever?

indicators.note: ending in means take the last letter of jail
getting no answer means the answer abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: to fear something is to be afraid of it

explanation.surface: A prisoner, unanswered, fears they will be inside for good.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing question, asked by a prisoner on a life sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence may well wonder if they will stay in prison permanently.

clue.text: Needs to be casual in speech

indicators.note: in speech means we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: lax means casual or slack

explanation.surface: One needs to be relaxed when talking.
explanation.definitionFit: If one lacks something, one needs or wants it, is without it.

clue.text: A rescue organised outside very quiet capital

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the very quiet symbol
organised means arranged afresh, so the letters of a rescue are reordered

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A rescue is arranged around a very quiet capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges A RESCUE into UERCASE, which goes 'outside' PP.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are also called upper-case, from the printers' top type tray.

clue.text: Mountains in pictures, miles away

indicators.note: away means the miles abbreviation goes, removed from the pictures

parts.note: murals are wall pictures

explanation.surface: Mountains shown in paintings, far off in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are a range in Russia dividing Europe from Asia.

clue.text: Cold girl getting degree, the heartless student you study with

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lass is a girl
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed

explanation.surface: A frosty girl with a degree, the cold-hearted student in your class.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the same form at school is a fellow pupil you learn alongside.

clue.text: Material in bathroom in short supply?

indicators.note: in short supply means the word for bathroom is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a toilet is a bathroom

explanation.surface: Cloth in the bathroom is running low, a toilet-roll crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a fabric, also a trial garment made of cheap cotton.

clue.text: Cuts of meat go bad aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means the spoiling word goes inside the steamship abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
eggs addle when they go bad

explanation.surface: The meat goes off on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle of lamb or venison is a joint cut from the back.

clue.text: A ceremony rendered by speaker correctly

indicators.note: rendered by speaker means the words are spoken and we hear them

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A ritual performed properly by the officiant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aright is an old adverb meaning rightly or without error.
